correctness.rationale: The map is identity inside the Euclidean unit ball and has derivative (I-uu^T)/r for x=ru, r>1; integrating derivatives along line segments and exterior r downarrow1 proves global equals sharp boundary Jacobian supremum in either fixed norm. A weighted infinity row sum for symmetric I-uu^T, Cauchy equality on off-row normal components, and the two-dimensional maximization yield (1+||w||2/w_i)/2, maximizing at minimal weight; weighted dual l1 has the same matrix norm. Independent 10,000 randomly weighted configurations verified maximizing row and column induced norms and explicit normals; n=1 and positive weights treated separately. Finite checks support but do not replace the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: Goebel (2003) treats retractions of an infinite-dimensional norm ball onto its sphere, a different map/domain, while the stated source for Su–Yu–Fei-Fei (2012) treats Euclidean projection algorithms rather than exact cross-norm sensitivity. Full Goebel paper was not accessible by permitted web view, so negative whole-document coverage is not asserted. Related published projection results concern nearest-point mapping onto weighted crosspolytopes or the Euclidean disk measured in a different l_p norm. The all-n anisotropically weighted Euclidean-ball to weighted-coordinate formula and maximizing normal classification were not identified; an equivalent older orthogonal hyperplane projector norm theorem remains an explicit originality risk.
residual_risks: Older matrix-theoretic orthogonal hyperplane projection norm calculations may supply an implication-equivalent cross-norm bound.

Finite dimensional real, strictly positive weights only; equality is boundary derivative limit, not distinct-point global Lipschitz pair.
